parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Choba-LawnTennisField, Lawn Tennis Field, University of Port Harcourt, Choba Town. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 91.2 | 2.535 | 2.535
2 | 380.2 | 15.83 | 18.37
3 | 43.25 | 20.36 | 38.73
4 | 474.3 | 33.05 | 71.78
5 | 597.1 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Choba-LawnTennisField, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Choba-LawnTennisField, Lawn Tennis Field, University of Port Harcourt, Choba Town**

The VES interpretation at this station reveals a five-layer subsurface sequence. Layer 1 is moderately resistive (91.2 Ω·m, 2.54 m thick), overlain by a more resistive Layer 2 (380.2 Ω·m, extending to 18.37 m depth). Layer 3 shows a marked drop in resistivity (43.25 Ω·m, down to 38.73 m), likely indicating a clayey or saturated horizon. Beneath this, resistivity rises sharply in Layer 4 (474.3 Ω·m, to 71.78 m) and continues increasing in the basal Layer 5 (597.1 Ω·m).

Applying the three-layer resistivity comparison rule sequentially:
- Layers 1-2-3: r1 < r2 > r3 → K
- Layers 2-3-4: r2 > r3 < r4 → H
- Layers 3-4-5: r3 < r4 < r5 → A

This yields a KHA-type curve, consistent with the on-file classification. No discrepancy was found between the computed curve type and the stated label.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
